key_insight: AIDE^2 shows that an AI research agent can recursively improve its own code, with each successful rewrite becoming the next version of the agent and yielding sustained gains.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path to automate agent R&D optimization, potentially reducing diminishing returns in research engineering while improving search, memory, and robustness.
method: The system generates candidate edits to the agent’s own code.
It benchmarks each modified agent on AI R&D tasks and keeps the best-performing changes using hidden evaluations.
Over an autonomous 8-day run, it discovered seven successive improvements, including new search policies and memory mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on four held-out benchmarks across ML engineering, heuristic algorithm engineering, and out-of-distribution weather forecasting, plus a separate task family where reward hacking fell from 55% to 32%.
watch_item: Results depend on hidden-evaluation selection and a specific agent/task setup, so transferability and safety under broader deployment still need careful verification.
paper_title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
